answer.answer: The NPS Vatsalya Scheme is a contributory saving and long-term financial security scheme designed exclusively for minors below 18 years of age [E01]. It was announced by the Finance Minister in the Union Budget for FY 2024-25 with the objective of nurturing a culture of savings from an early age, promoting financial literacy, and building a secure financial future for children [E01]. The scheme is regulated by the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) under the PFRDA Act, 2013 [E01]. Parents or guardians can open an NPS Vatsalya account for their children and contribute until the child reaches 18 years, with a minimum contribution of ₹250 per year and no limit on maximum contribution [E01]. Relatives and friends can also gift contributions to the account [E01]. Upon attainment of 18 years, the subscriber can continue under NPS Vatsalya for up to three years (till 21 years) unless they opt to exit or shift to another NPS model [E01]. Partial withdrawals up to 25% of contributions (excluding returns) are allowed after minimum 3 years for education, treatment of specified illnesses, or disability more than 75% [E01]. Upon exit at age 18 or later, up to 80% of accumulated corpus can be withdrawn as lump sum, with the balance used for annuity purchase [E03].
